final_rationale: The Actor did not provide genuinely new admissible evidence. The response mainly narrows and caveats the claim, which improves precision but does not close the initial compliance concerns. That distinction matters here: a caveated certification theory may be a more accurate business description of what leadership could choose to do, but it is not the same as evidence that the release is policy-compliant. The admissible record still shows a named launch use case below target, tied to customer commitments, under open legal review, with no evidence of disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance. Because those predicates remain unmet, the audit picture does not move to compliant or compliant_with_caveats. The proper final assessment remains suspicious rather than noncompliant because the record supports operational readiness and an unresolved materiality dispute, but does not support treating the dispute as closed.
remaining_concerns: A named launch use case still misses target by 2.1 percentage points, so the materiality trigger remains live under the stated policy.
The affected segment remains named in three international pilot commitments; the non-core or low-volume characterization does not close materiality on this record.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required is still open, so a required policy predicate remains unresolved.
There is still no admissible evidence of resolution, actual disclosure, or approved pre-launch risk acceptance covering the gap.
Aggregate readiness and deployment-stage monitoring support operational readiness only; they do not satisfy the disclosure-policy condition for a potentially material limitation.
